hasPart.description: Putting a heat pack or pack of frozen peas wrapped in a tea towel on your arm can help ease elbow and arm pain. You can also take painkillers.

hasPart.text:
To ease elbow and arm pain, try these things for a couple of days:

  • put a heat pack or a pack of frozen peas wrapped in a tea towel on your arm – do this for 10 to 15 minutes, every few hours
  • take painkillers like paracetamol or ibuprofen
  • raise your arm if it's swollen

hasPart.headline: How you can ease elbow and arm pain yourself
See a GP if:
hasPart.text:
• elbow or arm pain does not go away after a few weeks
Information:

Refer yourself for back or joint help

In many areas you may be able to get help, such as physiotherapy, from NHS community musculoskeletal (MSK) services without needing a referral from a GP.

Get NHS help for back or joint problems

hasPart.headline: Get help from NHS 111 if your arm:
hasPart.text:
• hurts when you exercise but the pain goes away when you rest
  • is swollen and you have a very high temperature, or feel hot, cold or shivery

Go to an urgent treatment centre or A&E if:

  • you have severe pain in your arm and it's difficult to move
  • you've injured your arm and you heard a snapping noise or your arm has changed shape
  • your arm tingles or feels numb

hasPart.headline: Call 999 if:
hasPart.text:
• arm pain has come on suddenly and it occurs with pressure, heaviness or squeezing across your chest

This could be a sign of a heart attack .

hasPart.description: Possible causes of elbow and arm pain include tendonitis, sprains and strains, frozen shoulder, arthritis and bursitis.

Do not self-diagnose. See a GP if you're worried.

sections.heading: Causes of elbow and arm pain

headings.text: Causes of elbow and arm pain

sections.text:
Causes of elbow and arm pain
Apart from an injury, these things can cause arm and elbow pain.
Do not self-diagnose. See a GP if you're worried.
Common causes of elbow and arm pain
Main symptoms
Possible cause
Pain on the outside of the elbow, difficulty to fully extend the arm
Tennis elbow
Joint pain, stiffness, swelling, difficulty moving the affected area
Tendonitis
or
bursitis
Pain, tenderness, bruising, swelling
Sprains and strains
Pain, stiffness coming down from the shoulder
Frozen shoulder
Pain and stiffness in the joints
Arthritis
Swelling around a joint and a high temperature (or you feel hot, cold or shivery)
Joint infection (
septic arthritis
)
